items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: he was trying to sing his way back home to Dixie, his wife

ctx.x: He'd be appearing somewhere in town, in a picture or theater or something. But we would always know that he was going to be there and we'd play for him right off the top of our heads. Whatever he wanted to play, we'd do those things. Mildred Bailey used to come by when she first came out with Paul Whiteman. She used to come by and sit and sing with us. All of the good stars, they came into that place because that was the top nightclub of the West and it was during

Prohibition time and that was one of the few places where you could go and find a first-class nightclub that went on until four and five o'clock in the morning. After everything was over in Hollywood at the Coconut Grove, they started heading toward the Apex. That's where it was. That was just a little bit before Bing Crosby went to work in the Coconut Grove with Gus Arnheim (PHONETIC). I was working at the Sebastian's Hide Cotton Club with Les Haight (PHONETIC) at the time that Bing Crosby was doing his --…

As a matter of fact, I was fortunate enough to appear with one of Bing's last concerts, at the Concord Jazz up in Concord, California, two months ago, right before he went on his European tour. So, seeing that he just passed last week, I think it was a very fortunate thing to be able to be a part of him again in his waning days. He was a pretty good man, as singers go.
